item.text: I found further specific connections in the bone and sinew imagery, reciprocal counsel, patient work, and the consequences of building unjustly. I’ll save only those new proposals to the follow-up TSV.

item.command:
/bin/bash -lc "cat > '/Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec12/sol/followup.tsv' <<'EOF'
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Job.10.11	skin as clothing; bones and sinews knit together	The commentary combines tightly woven fabric with the place where bones meet; Job addresses God as the one who clothed him with skin and flesh and knit him together with bones and sinews, giving both images one bodily setting.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.37.7	bone joined to its bone	The source's حق can mean where two bones meet and its counsel joins separated pieces; Ezekiel reports that at the prophetic word the scattered bones came together, bone to its bone, before the bodies lived.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.37.11	dry bones; lost hope; cut off	The commentary sets joining and repair against loss and severance; the exiles identify themselves as dry bones and say their hope is lost and they are cut off, making the physical reunion of verse 7 answer a declared communal loss.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.139.15	frame intricately woven	The commentary puts tightly woven fabric beside the meeting of bones; the psalmist describes his bodily frame as intricately woven while hidden in formation, a creation image rather than a moral construction.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Eccl.4.9	two workers and reward for toil	The commentary makes mutual joining and useful work answer loss; Ecclesiastes says two are better than one because their labor has a good reward, grounding the lifting and unbreakable cord described in the following verses.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.27.17	iron sharpens iron; person sharpens person	The commentary's tavsiye is reciprocal counsel that strengthens a structure; Proverbs describes one person sharpening another as iron sharpens iron, making mutual improvement a material image.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.11.3	foundations destroyed; plight of righteous	The commentary distinguishes the sound foundation from the one that collapses; the psalm asks what the righteous can do if foundations are destroyed, making structural failure an ethical crisis.
strong	tevrat	motif	WLC:Amos.9.11	raise fallen shelter; repair breaches	The commentary defines صالح as repairing damage and presents a secure house as its product; God promises to raise David's fallen booth and repair its breaches, making restoration of a ruined dwelling explicit.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Isa.53.11	ع م ل / Hebrew עמל, table sound correspondence	The commentary asks whether work can answer loss through righteousness; Isaiah's servant comes through the toil of his soul to an outcome that makes many righteous, linking the cognate for painful effort to a fruitful result in this verse's own servant context.
strong	tevrat	soydas	WLC:Jer.31.36	ح ق ق / Hebrew חקק, table sound correspondence	The source sets firm حق beside a covenant that can be broken; Jeremiah says that if God's fixed cosmic statutes depart, Israel will cease as a people, using the cognate for enduring ordinances to secure the restored relationship.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Col.2.2	hearts encouraged and knit together in love	The commentary makes reciprocal counsel join parts into one whole; Paul seeks encouraged hearts joined together in love as they reach assured understanding, giving verbal support and cohesion one purpose.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1John.3.18	deed and truth together	The commentary joins firm truthful speech to constructive works; the letter urges love in deed and truth rather than words alone, making both elements necessary to a real bond.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.9	persist in doing good until harvest	The ayah joins good deeds with mutual counsel in patience; Galatians tells the community not to tire of doing good because a harvest comes if they do not give up, giving endurance a concrete gain.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.15.58	steadfast labor not in vain	The commentary opposes durable, beneficial work to loss; Paul calls believers steadfast and abundant in the Lord's work because their labor is not vain, joining firmness, work, and gain.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:2Thess.3.13	do not tire of doing good	The commentary makes righteous work something held together by patience; the letter directly tells brothers not to grow weary in doing good, identifying fatigue as a threat to the work.
strong	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Rom.2.7	patience in good work	The surah names good deeds and patient exhortation as the exception to loss; Paul describes those who persist in good work seeking glory and receiving eternal life, linking sustained action to its outcome.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.139.13	body knit in the womb	The source's woven fabric and joined bones picture sound formation; the psalmist says God knit him in his mother's womb, giving the textile image a personal bodily origin.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ezek.37.8	joined bodies still lacking breath	The commentary treats joined pieces as part of restoration; Ezekiel sees sinews, flesh, and skin cover the assembled bones, yet says there is no breath in them, qualifying how far physical reconstruction alone goes.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.90.17	work of hands made firm	The commentary wants labor to yield a durable structure rather than loss under time; the prayer asks God to establish the work of human hands, directly turning transient toil into a request for permanence.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Jer.22.13	unjust house built with unpaid labor	The source uses a builder's bricklaying for صالح deeds; Jeremiah condemns the man who builds his house unjustly by making a neighbor work without wages, showing that successful construction can embody corruption.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Amos.5.11	stone houses built but not inhabited	The commentary contrasts sound building with loss; Amos tells oppressors that although they built houses of dressed stone they will not live in them, linking unjust work to forfeited shelter.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.2.12	city built with bloodshed	The commentary's joined building signifies beneficial action; Habakkuk pronounces woe on the person who builds a town with blood, making the shared construction harmful through its means.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Hab.2.13	peoples labor for fire and nothing	The commentary sets constructive work against loss; the next verse says peoples toil only for fire and weary themselves for nothing, giving the unjust city's building its fruitless end.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Gen.11.8	Babel builders scattered	The earlier Babel scene joins people around brickmaking and a tower; God disperses the builders over the earth, completing the counterexample to the commentary's beneficial joining.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.4.9	hands lay foundation and finish house	The commentary's work places bricks into a sound whole; Zechariah says Zerubbabel's hands laid the temple foundation and will complete it, keeping beginning and completion in the same laboring hands.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Isa.61.4	rebuild ruins and repair devastated cities	The commentary describes صالح as repair after spoilage; Isaiah says the restored people will rebuild ancient ruins and repair devastated cities, making collective recovery a construction task.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.119.142	enduring righteousness and truthful instruction	The commentary gives حق the force of something firm and rightly set; the psalm joins God's everlasting righteousness to instruction that is truth, linking durability and moral truth without the fabric metaphor.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Ps.119.160	truthful word and enduring judgments	The source calls a well-formed utterance firm; the psalm says the sum of God's word is truth and every righteous judgment endures, locating verbal soundness in permanence.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.11	word suited to its setting	The source compares sound speech with a door's foot fitting its socket; Proverbs likens a word spoken at the right time to gold apples in silver settings, giving apt placement an image of material fit.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Prov.25.12	wise rebuke fitted to listening ear	The commentary's counsel must attach person to person; Proverbs pairs a wise reprover with an ear that listens, comparing the encounter to a gold ornament, so the fit depends on receiving speech.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.11.10	broken staff annulled covenant	The commentary quotes a divine covenant broken after being bound; Zechariah enacts the opposite direction when the shepherd breaks his staff and thereby annuls his covenant, making the actor and direction of rupture distinct.
medium	tevrat	motif	WLC:Zech.11.14	broken staff annuls brotherhood	The commentary says cutting what ought to be joined leads to loss; the shepherd breaks a second staff to annul the brotherhood between Judah and Israel, an enacted severance of a social bond.
medium	tevrat	yorum_gelenegi	Pirkei Avot 1:17	practice greater than exposition	The commentary insists that firm words become useful through deeds; this teaching says practice is the main thing rather than exposition and cautions against multiplying words, sharpening the distinction between sound speech and empty talk.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.2	patience while bearing one another	The commentary's reciprocal joining must endure strain; Ephesians asks believers to bear with one another in love with humility, gentleness, and patience before urging unity.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Eph.4.3	unity kept in a bond of peace	The source says recommendation attaches one part to another; Ephesians directs believers to maintain the Spirit's unity in the bond of peace, expressing an ethical joining before its jointed-body image.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.9	coworkers and God's building	The commentary turns individual works into a collective building; Paul calls his fellow ministers God's coworkers and the community God's building, identifying both laborers and structure.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.11	foundation that cannot be replaced	The source compares secure and collapsing foundations; Paul says no one can lay a foundation other than Jesus Christ, specifying why the community's building can be sound.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:1Cor.3.12	contrasting materials laid on foundation	The commentary's firm fabric and sound bricks imply that materials matter; Paul lists lasting and combustible materials a builder might place on the foundation, preparing for the fire test in the next verse.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Heb.10.36	endurance after doing God's will	The ayah names patience alongside good action; Hebrews says believers need endurance so that, having done God's will, they receive the promise, tying perseverance to completed action.
medium	incil	motif	SBLGNT:Gal.6.10	do good especially to faith's household	The commentary treats righteous work as building a community; Galatians urges doing good to everyone, especially the household of faith, identifying the circle in which the work strengthens bonds.
medium	incil	motif	Shepherd of Hermas, Vision 3.3	stones rejected from the tower	The commentary's building holds only when its joined pieces are sound; Hermas's tower vision sets rejected stones beside stones incorporated into it, making the fitness of each component morally consequential.
medium	incil	motif	1 Clement 37:5	small and great bodily members together	The source compares mutual counsel to parts joined in a body; Clement's discussion of members says the body requires both small and great parts to function together, extending the anatomical image to church order.
medium	incil	motif	1 Clement 38:1	strong provide for weak	The commentary's good deeds attach people and repair what is weak; Clement asks strong members to care for weak members and rich ones to supply the poor, giving the jointed body a practical obligation.
medium	incil	motif	Ignatius, Ephesians 9:1	believers as stones of Father's temple	The commentary builds a sound structure from its believers' deeds; Ignatius pictures his addressees as stones of the Father's temple raised by the cross, with faith and love involved in their movement.
EOF"

item.text: Saved new proposals to [followup.tsv](/Volumes/aro/projects/prose_generation/enrichment/bible/work/s103/discovery/s103-20261009/sec12/sol/followup.tsv). Accuracy concern: these are memory-based candidates; the nonbiblical section citations need verification.
